clue.text: Contribution to disorder as calculating mischief-maker

indicators.note: a contribution is a small part handed over, so the answer is a part taken from the words that follow

parts.note: runs across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A scheming troublemaker is credited with adding to the general chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'as' looks like a link word joining definition and wordplay, but it sits inside the run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a mischievous rogue, so the word is a straight synonym for a troublemaker.

clue.text: Banking on weapon that's protecting one

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: something protecting another wraps around it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a lance is a long weapon used by knights
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A knight counts on a weapon guarding him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banking on' wants to be the definition as one phrase; 'on' is split off as wordplay, leaving 'Banking' as in banking on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliance is dependence or trust, the noun for what you are doing when you bank on something.

clue.text: Mix of fuels for light baking

indicators.note: a mix is a blend in which ingredients lose their order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A blend of fuels is recommended for gentle oven work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' looks like a joining word but supplies two letters of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A soufflé is an airy baked dish of whisked egg whites, so it is light baking in the literal sense.

clue.text: A line separating country in Europe and another

indicators.note: something separating a thing goes between its parts, so one piece splits another

parts.note: Austria is a central European country
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: A border divides a European nation from its neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' refers back to 'country': the answer is a second, non-European country.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a country too, so it is another country besides the European one named in the clue.

clue.text: I play-act in silly way that's unusual

indicators.note: doing something in a silly way means doing it foolishly and out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor admits that hamming it up foolishly is out of character.
explanation.definitionFit: Something atypical is not representative of its type, which is a close synonym for out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Movement that's raised skill and physical activity in people

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word lifts it so it reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of conversation

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so a piece goes within the final word

parts.note: a nation is a people
sport is physical activity

explanation.surface: A popular campaign that has boosted craft and exercise among the population.
explanation.walkthrough: The sport goes inside the nation after its first letter, giving N-SPORT-ATION, all following the backwards skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Transportation is the movement of people or goods from one place to another.

clue.text: Epitome of stiffness in game

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the fireside iron in the idiom stiff as one
second meaning: a card game played for stakes

explanation.surface: A player is the very model of rigidity during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'stiff as a poker' makes the fire iron the standard image of rigidity.
explanation.definitionFit: A poker is a rigid metal rod for stirring a fire and also the card game of betting and bluffing.

clue.text: Turn over detail of school uniform that gives head fit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: overturn, as a boat does

definitions.text: detail of school uniform that gives head fit
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: the measurement that makes a school hat fit

explanation.surface: An instruction to check the label on a school hat for the size.
explanation.walkthrough: Split it into two words to read the second meaning: the measurement of a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: To capsize is to overturn in water, and read as two words it is the measurement of a cap that makes it fit.

clue.text: Little pigs, for example, create untidiness

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a group of young born to one mother at the same time

explanation.surface: Piglets make a mess, as piglets do.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter is a brood of young animals such as piglets, and to litter is to strew rubbish around.

clue.text: Drink after first piece reduces energy — that limits star's appearance

indicators.note: one thing coming after another follows it, so the drink is placed behind the piece

parts.note: Part I is the first part of a work
ale is a drink
to clip is to cut back or reduce
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A drinker finds the first pint saps their energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First piece' means Part I. The star whose appearance is limited is the sun, partly obscured by the moon.
explanation.definitionFit: In a partial eclipse the moon covers only some of the sun, so the star is seen only in part.

clue.text: From which you might get oil in USA — area that's near Mississippi

definitions.text: From which you might get oil in USA — area that's near Mississippi

indicators.note: the answer is the source that these letters can be got out of by rearranging, so the anagram works from answer to clue words

parts.note: taken as written
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A description of an oil-producing American region next to the Mississippi.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description: rearranging the state's letters yields OIL IN USA plus A for area, and the state does produce oil and borders Mississippi.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana is a US state with major petroleum reserves that lies beside the state of Mississippi and at the river's mouth.

clue.text: Broken article placed on end of desk

indicators.note: in a down clue placing something on another means putting it after, so the wordplay pieces follow the kept letter
the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of desk is kept

parts.note: last letter of the word
A is the indefinite article
put means placed

explanation.surface: Something set down at the far end of a desk has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: KAPUT comes from German and is informal for broken or finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Kaput is an informal adjective for something no longer working, a synonym for broken.

clue.text: Trees planted in middle of Seattle, initially

indicators.note: things planted in soil are set inside it, so one piece goes inside another
the middle of a word is its central portion, so only the inner letters of the city name are kept

parts.note: the central three letters of the seven-letter city name
firs are a kind of tree

explanation.surface: Seattle's first trees were planted in the city centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trees planted in middle of Seattle' reads like a news item about urban greening; the comma separates the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: At first is an adverbial phrase meaning at the beginning, which is what initially means.

clue.text: Waiting for start of action in court

definitions.meaning: first meaning: waiting at table, attending to customers in a restaurant
second meaning: the stroke that starts each point in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone waits for a legal case to begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, but it is a tennis court, where each rally begins with this stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Waiting staff provide service at table, and in tennis the service is the opening shot of each point.

clue.text: It contains what's caught with fishing equipment

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a basket that holds the catch
second meaning: an item of an angler's kit

explanation.surface: Something holds the fish an angler has landed along with the rest of the tackle.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket an angler carries to hold caught fish, part of the gear taken on a trip.

clue.text: Diagnose wrongly, hence intensely worried

indicators.note: doing something wrongly means getting it out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor's misdiagnosis leaves the patient deeply anxious.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonised means suffering great mental anguish, which matches being extremely worried.

clue.text: Haughty and irreverent around ruler

indicators.note: one thing around another encircles it, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: impious means lacking reverence
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A description of someone proud and disrespectful in the presence of a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual crossword ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperious means domineering and arrogant, close in sense to haughty.

clue.text: Mint and cinnamon, finally, included in concoction

indicators.note: something included in another is put inside it, so pieces go within the last word

parts.note: a brew is a concoction
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word just before it

parts.note: last letter of the spice

explanation.surface: A recipe in which mint and cinnamon go into a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mint' looks like the herb in a spiced drink, but it means in perfect new condition, as in mint condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint as an adjective means unused and pristine, like a freshly struck coin, which is brand-new.

clue.text: A couple of pages are not clear

parts.note: taken as written
p is page, so two of them are PP, as in reference abbreviations
taken as written
NT is a contracted form of not, as in can't

explanation.surface: A reader complains that two pages of a text are confusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not clear' reads as a complaint, but 'not' belongs to the wordplay and 'clear' alone is the definition, the opposite of the surface meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means plainly visible or obvious, a synonym of clear.

clue.text: Loyal citizen in disturbance after non-violent strike

indicators.note: one thing coming after another follows it, so the disturbance is placed behind the strike

parts.note: a pat is a gentle tap
a riot is a violent public disturbance

explanation.surface: A law-abiding person caught up in unrest following a peaceful walkout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-violent strike' suggests industrial action, but it is a light blow with the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot is someone devoted to their country, which a loyal citizen is.

clue.text: Person still being portrayed as problem

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who sits motionless for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: A sitter whose portrait is still unfinished is proving troublesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like 'yet', but it means motionless: the model holds a pose.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is one who poses, such as an artist's model, and also a difficult question or puzzle.

clue.text: Servile as prodigal son, to begin with

indicators.note: something put in to begin with goes at the front, so this piece leads

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
prodigal means extravagant or lavish

explanation.surface: The prodigal son of the parable began by grovelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls the Biblical Prodigal Son, but 'prodigal' is just a synonym for lavish.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavish means submissively obedient, like a slave, which is what servile describes.

clue.text: Talk informally about fellow in taxi

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so pieces go within the vehicle

parts.note: a cab is a taxi
on means about, as in a talk on art
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: Chatting casually about a man riding in a taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: To confab is to chat, from confabulate, an informal word for having a conversation.

clue.text: In new form, I am top learner, as good as can be

indicators.note: something put into a new form is remade in a different shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A pupil boasts of being top of the class and at peak performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal means best or most favourable, the highest level something can reach.

clue.text: Characteristic of feet as measure of length

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the rhythm of poetry built from metrical feet
second meaning: the metric unit of distance

explanation.surface: A comparison of imperial feet with a metric measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feet' suggests the unit of length, but here it means poetic feet, the units of rhythm in verse.
explanation.definitionFit: Metre is the rhythmic pattern formed by feet in verse, and also the SI unit of length.

clue.text: Country in the grip of winter rainstorm

indicators.note: being in the grip of something means being held inside it, so the answer lies within the words that follow

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A nation is held fast by a wintry downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' suggests a nation, but here it means land or landscape, as in open country.
explanation.definitionFit: Country in the sense of a stretch of land with particular features is a synonym for terrain.

clue.text: Loud, isn't hard to hear

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A paradoxical remark that something loud is not difficult to make out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to say the sound is easily heard, but 'Loud' and 'isn't' are both wordplay, leaving only 'hard to hear' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A faint sound is weak and barely audible, which is what hard to hear describes.

clue.text: Step up on one side of debate

parts.note: pro means in favour, one side of an argument
the motion is the proposal under debate

explanation.surface: A speaker advances by arguing for one side in a formal debate.
explanation.walkthrough: In a formal debate, the motion is the proposition argued over, with speakers pro and con.
explanation.definitionFit: A promotion is an advance in rank or position, a step up the ladder at work.

clue.text: Was a pest of different type found in part of garden?

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a flower bed is a part of a garden
other means different or of another kind

explanation.surface: A question about whether an unusual garden creature in the flower bed was a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: To have bothered someone is to have annoyed or troubled them, as a pest does.

clue.text: Avoid or escape key cut

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Advice on dodging an escape key that has been removed from a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To eschew something is to deliberately abstain from it, a formal synonym of avoid.
